opportunities.title: 678,000 French Taxpayers Just Got Doxxed to Crypto Wrench Gangs
opportunities.why_now: A government tax leak just handed physical-attack targeting lists to criminals, and Coldcard losses already top $150M this year — the two stories are the same story.
opportunities.angle: Investigative explainer connecting the French breach to the ongoing wrench-attack wave, with concrete OPSEC steps (custody splitting, plausible deniability wallets, doxxing hygiene) — 'the state can leak you even if you never got hacked'

opportunities.title: Coldcard's $150M Problem: When the 'Secure' Wallet Becomes the Attack Vector
opportunities.why_now: Galaxy's new estimate puts Coldcard-linked losses over $150M, a number big enough to force a hard look at hardware-wallet trust assumptions.
opportunities.angle: Security teardown: what actually went wrong (supply chain? seed extraction? social engineering?), scored against a 'self-custody checklist' — skeptical, not promotional

opportunities.title: Tether Got Its First Audit and Still Won't Show You the Statements
opportunities.why_now: KPMG signed off on Tether's first full audit but the underlying statements weren't published, and CEO Ardoino's 'I don't care' response is doing the rounds today.
opportunities.angle: Skeptic's ledger: what an audit without disclosure actually proves (not much) — a checklist of what real transparency would require, aimed at readers who've heard 'audited' promises before

opportunities.title: The $11.8M LinkedIn Job Offer: Inside Singapore's Crypto Recruiter Scam Wave
opportunities.why_now: Singapore just tallied $11.8M in losses from fake crypto job offers on LinkedIn, a vector that's scaling fast and hitting technically sophisticated targets.
opportunities.angle: Anatomy-of-a-scam piece: how the fake recruiter pipeline works step by step (interview → 'coding test' → malware/wallet drain), with a spot-the-signs checklist for anyone job-hunting in crypto

opportunities.title: Ireland Wants 'Enhanced Checks' on Your Private Wallet — Here's What That Actually Means
opportunities.why_now: Ireland's new AML strategy explicitly targets self-custodied wallets just as self-custody incidents (French leak, Coldcard losses) dominate headlines, setting up a security-vs-surveillance collision.
opportunities.angle: Policy-meets-security analysis: does state wallet surveillance make holders safer or just create a bigger honeypot/target list — framed for readers who already distrust both hackers and regulators equally
